title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (October 2026 data) — 9:00 a.m. ET, the pre-open half of a two-index house-price morning this calendar currently tracks only half of
source: EST: derived from the publisher's own stated schedule rule, read direct from a primary today. press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 90,693 bytes), states it verbatim: `The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET.` December 2026's Tuesdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, so the last is 2026-12-29. The same release's own two-month reporting lag (published 2026-08-25, reporting June data) puts October 2026 data in the 2026-12-29 slot. This is the SAME primary and the SAME derivation this calendar's existing case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27 entry was filed against, re-read today rather than carried. Corroborated structurally by this calendar itself: fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 and consumer-confidence-2026-12-29 are already tracked on that date, and the two house-price indices have shared a 9:00am morning in every month this calendar carries both. Filed estimate on three counts: the schedule is derived from a stated RULE rather than read off a published December date, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a private index publisher, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-09 by the treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 never-assessed initial research, at D+1 of its corridor. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: this calendar tracks case-shiller-hpi-2026-09-29 and case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27 and then jumps to case-shiller-hpi-2027-02-23 — November and December 2026 are both missing, and December falls inside this sweep's corridor. The asymmetry is the tell: fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 IS tracked, so the calendar currently sees one half of a two-index house-price morning and not the other, which is exactly the shape of gap the 2026-11-23 sibling filled when it found the Thanksgiving half-day tracked with no full closure in front of it. WHY IT EARNS A ROW BEYOND SYMMETRY: it is one more entry in the D+1 crowd (7-Year auction, consumer confidence, FHFA HPI, and the two Dallas Fed surveys this sweep proposes) that makes the proposing event's central attribution limit visible rather than inferred. NOT PROPOSED, AND THE REASON IS RECORDED: chicago-pmi-2026-12-31 is the other obvious gap in this corridor — the series is tracked for 2026-09-30, 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-30 and stops, and the publisher's rule (last business day of the month at 09:45 ET) puts December on 2026-12-31, inside the corridor. Both attempts to read that rule from its own primary failed today (mnimarkets.com/chicago-business-barometer HTTP 404; /products/chicago-business-barometer HTTP 307 redirecting to the site root), so it is recorded in the proposing ledger's probe-ref `blocked` array and left for a session that can reach the source, rather than filed off a sibling entry's transcription.
